messages:
anya: Heads-up — we got a cluster spike that looks correlated to Xid 13 and Xid 79 on a small cohort of nv79 hosts in us-east-1 around 14:04-14:10. Tenant appears to be an embeddings-heavy job doing large-batch prefix caching (edgebox-prod).

mike: Can you paste the logs? any ECC entries or thermal warnings?

anya: Paste below (trimmed):
```
Mar 10 14:05:12 nv79-23 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 13, pid=8742, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 10 14:05:12 nv79-23 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 79, pid=8742, GPU reported ECC error
Mar 10 14:06:08 nv79-23 user: embedding_worker[8742]: failed batch (batch_size=96, seq=512) -> runtime error: nvml: ECC event
```

anya: No raw ECC counters in syslog beyond that. nvidia-smi shows driver 535.x, CUDA 12.1. We pushed an int8-optimized kernel for the new quantized embedder last week.

lee: Interesting — batch_size=96 + seq=512 is a pretty bad shape for nv79 thermal throttling when multiple workloads are colocated. Is the workload using NVLink P2P or large pinned host buffers?

anya: edgebox uses P2P to scatter embeddings across two GPUs for sharded embedding table lookups. NVLink was up but perftop showed occasional link re-negotiation around the time.

olivia: Did we auto-batch this tenant? That many concurrent requests + continuous KV cache could blow the power cap or cause PCI resets.

anya: They were on dedicated pool but autoscale allowed burst into shared hosts for spikes. Affected hosts were in the shared pool (pool-shared-3).

mike: Actionable check list: 1) mark nv79-23 & nv79-27 for immediate drain; 2) collect full dmesg + nvecc counters; 3) rollback the new int8 kernel on a canary node and repro.

lee: I already queued drains: `fleetctl drain nv79-23 nv79-27 --reason "xid13-79 correlation"`

infra-bot: Deploy task created: DR-4123, owner=@mike, priority=high

mike: I'll grab dmesg + nvml logs. Running: `sudo cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log /var/log/dmesg | sed -n '1,200p'` and `python /opt/tools/nvccounters.py --host nv79-23 --since 14:00`

anya: One more datapoint: this tenant's recent change switched from 4-token prompt buckets to dynamic 512 seq padding to optimize embedding alignment. That increases memory working set and reduces KV cache hits for other jobs.

olivia: Could be memory fragmentation -> driver alloc + ECC bounce -> Xid 79. Also Xid 13 can be from illegal memory access if the int8 pack kernel has edge cases with odd sequence lengths.

mike: I repro'd locally on a dev nv79 replica by running their embedding harness with batch_size=96, seq=512 + our int8 kernel. I got a GPU reset and Xid 13 after ~120s. Stack trace points at our fused pack/unpack kernel (embed_pack.cu:line 212).

lee: Good repro. Can you capture a repro trace with CUPTI + nsys and attach? We need to know whether it's a driver bug, kernel out-of-bounds, or thermal/power.

mike: Uploaded trace to S3: s3://redwood-traces/DR-4123/nv79-pack-repro-176892. Nsight shows a device-side memcopy failing just before reset. No temperature spike before reset — temps ~72C. Power readings show short power draw spike to 290W (powercap=300W).

olivia: Powercap headroom small but within limit. Short spike to 290W shouldn't trigger reset. Memory writes out-of-bounds sounds more like a kernel bug. Could the int8 path be indexing with 32-bit offsets that overflow at high seq*batch?

mike: I found code: `int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; if (idx < seq_len * batch) { ... }` but seq_len*batch is computed as signed 32-bit and sometimes wrapped on larger batches -> negative checks pass -> OOB. Patch suggested: use 64-bit index.

anya: Nice catch. That explains Xid 13 (illegal memory access). How do we explain Xid 79 (ECC) though?

lee: OOB writes can corrupt ECC-protected memory and flip bits; driver may report ECC events if memory corruption touches ECC-protected regions. Also GPU reset after OOB could surface as Xid 79 in combination.

mike: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) revert int8 fused kernel on shared pool images; 2) enforce tenant burst into shared pool forbidden for edgebox until patch lands; 3) run a 64-bit index build and test.

olivia: Agree. Also add a rollout guard: if batch_size*seq_len > 20M tokens, route to dedicated hosts or set smaller batch cap.

sre-oncall: I'll put temporary tenant throttles in place and add a firmware/driver check to detect similar patterns. Also add an alert rule for simultaneous Xid 13+79 within 5m on same pci bus.

anya: I've submitted a rollback and tenant throttle PRs: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/PRs/8791 (revert int8 pack), https://git.redwood/infrastructure/PRs/8792 (tenant burst cap).

mike: I'll prepare a proper fix (cast to int64_t for index computations) and run CI + local nv79 soak.

lee: Postmortem TODOs: - correlate past month for same kernel signoffs and any silent ECC increments - add unit test for large seq*batch cases - add per-tenant batch*seq telemetry to Console.

anya: Can we also add an automated canary that runs a synthetic embedder with edge-case dims on every new kernel rollout?

mike: Yeah, add to CI: `./ci/run-embedder-canary --batch 96 --seq 512 --repeat 1000`

olivia: Will follow up with a KCS ticket if vendor driver team wants traces.

anya: Thanks all. For now drains are in progress and tenant burst is disabled. I'll update DR-4123 with final RCA after mike's patch lands. :white_check_mark:
